get.description: List the SocialAccounts this API key is allowed to act on.

Newest first (by creation time). Only posts whose every platform target is on the key's account allowlist are returned. `status` and `social_account_id` must hold on the same platform target. `date_from`/`date_to` bound the post's date: when it goes out, or when it was created while it has no schedule. `tag` is an exact tag name; `search` matches the caption or title. When `next_cursor` is non-null, pass it back as `cursor`.

post.summary: Upload a new media asset (multipart form data)
post.description:
Upload a binary into the workspace's media library.

Body is ``multipart/form-data`` because agents posting videos can't
cleanly base64-encode 100 MB into JSON. MCP gets a separate
``upload_media`` tool that accepts base64 for small files (≤5 MB).

``alt_text`` / ``title`` / ``folder_id`` / ``tags`` are optional and
persisted alongside the asset, saving the agent a follow-up PATCH.
``tags`` is a CSV ("hero,launch") because multipart can't carry JSON
arrays cleanly.

parameters.name: actor_type
parameters.description: `human`, `agent` or `system`.

parameters.name: action_type

parameters.name: decision
parameters.description: `executed`, `held` or `blocked`.

get.description: The workspace's own values, with blanks filled from the organization's. Needs `create_posts` or `manage_workspace_settings`.

patch.description: Needs `manage_workspace_settings`. Fields you leave out are unchanged; lists replace.

get.description: Channels, workspaces, team members, scheduled posts this month and API & MCP calls today, each with its limit (`null` = unlimited). Self-hosted installs report `billing_enabled: false` and no limits.
Who is on the workspace's team, with their role and the `@mention` handle that notifies them from a comment. Email addresses are not included.

char_limit.description: Maximum caption length the platform accepts. Reject locally before calling /posts.

escaped_chars.description: Characters the platform requires escaped, each costing two against ``char_limit``. LinkedIn escapes its reserved little-text set, so count a caption as ``len(caption) + sum(caption.count(c) for c in escaped_chars)`` before rejecting it. Empty for platforms that publish the caption verbatim.

caption_counting.description: How the platform counts a caption against ``char_limit``. ``characters``: one per character (plus ``escaped_chars``). ``weighted``: the twitter-text v3 weighted count X uses, where each URL counts as 23 and CJK characters and emoji as 2.

needs_title.description: True when the platform requires a title (YouTube, Pinterest). When false, the title field is ignored.

supports_first_comment.description: True when the platform can auto-post a first comment after publish. False for TikTok, Pinterest, Bluesky, Google Business. LinkedIn Personal returns false when authorized via OIDC instead of the Community Management API. If false, ``first_comment`` is silently dropped at publish time.

requires_video.description: True when the platform publishes only video (TikTok, YouTube). Scheduling a post with no video in ``media_asset_ids`` is rejected with 422.

requires_media.description: True when the platform can't publish text alone (Instagram, Pinterest, and the ``requires_video`` platforms). Scheduling a post with no ``media_asset_ids`` is rejected with 422.

thread_mode.description: How the platform publishes a post's ``parts``: ``reply_chain`` replies each part to the one before it (Bluesky, Threads, Mastodon); ``comments`` posts later parts as comments on the first post (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube); ``none`` can't take a thread, and a post with ``parts`` is rejected with 422 when scheduled.

thread_max_parts.description: Most parts one thread may have, the first post included.

thread_part_max_length.description: Characters each later part may carry, counted like ``char_limit``.

thread_media_per_part.description: True when a later part can carry its own ``media_asset_ids``. Comments are text only.

post_settings.description: Per-post settings the platform needs beyond the caption (Reddit: ``subreddit``, ``flair_id``, ...). Each has a ``key``, ``label``, ``kind`` (text, select, checkbox), ``required`` and ``help``. Send them as ``post_settings`` when creating the post; a scheduled post missing a required one is rejected with 422.

MeResponse.description: Echoes everything the key is scoped to so an agent can self-introspect.

plan_slug.description: IntelligenceSubscription plan slug; empty if no active subscription.

AutonomyNotice.description: What the workspace's autonomy policy did with an agent's write, and what happens next.

decision.description: `executed`, `held` (saved as a draft for review) or `blocked`.

level.description: The autonomy level the decision was made under.

reasons.description: Why it was held or blocked.

message.description: A sentence you can act on or relay to the user.

undo_until.description: Until when a person can still undo it, if it can be undone.

PlatformPostPartSummary.description: One thread part's outcome on one account.

status.description: pending, posting, published, failed, or unconfirmed.

thread_status.description: none, pending, complete, or partial. ``partial`` means the first post and some parts are live and the thread stopped; POST /posts/{id}/resume-thread picks it up from the stopped part.

post_settings.description: The per-post settings this account's platform declares, as saved.

parts.description: The thread's later parts, in order. Empty for a single post.

recurrence.description: The repeat this post starts, if it is the first post of an active series.

recurrence_source_id.description: For a copy generated by a series: the series' first post, where its repeat is changed.

autonomy.description: Set on writes by an agent: whether the autonomy policy executed, held or blocked it, and why.

summary.description: The rule in words, e.g. "Every Tuesday and Thursday until 31 Dec".

position.description: 2 for the part right after the post, and so on.

CreatePostRequest.description:
Create a draft or directly schedule a post against one account.

``social_account_id`` MUST be in the key's allowlist; the auth class
raises 403 otherwise.

social_account_id.description: ID of the SocialAccount to target. Must be in the key's allowlist.

title.description: Required on platforms where ``needs_title=true`` (YouTube, Pinterest). Ignored otherwise.

first_comment.description: Auto-posted as a reply ~120s after the main post lands. Silently dropped at publish time when the target account's ``supports_first_comment`` is false (TikTok, Pinterest, Bluesky, Google Business; LinkedIn Personal in OIDC mode).

internal_notes.description: Private team-only note. Never published to any platform; surfaced only to your team via the API and the composer.

media_asset_ids.description: MediaAsset IDs already uploaded to the workspace's media library. Position-ordered.

platform_overrides.description: Optional per-platform overrides of title / caption / first_comment. Each entry's social_account_id must equal the post's social_account_id in the current single-account API. Sending a field as ``null`` (or omitting it) leaves the post's default in place for that platform.

parts.description: Optional later parts of a thread, in order; the post itself is the first part. Each account publishes them according to its ``thread_mode`` (see /accounts). Scheduling is rejected with 422 when an account can't publish the thread: ``thread_mode='none'``, more than ``thread_max_parts``, a part over ``thread_part_max_length``, or media on a part where ``thread_media_per_part`` is false.

post_settings.description: Per-post settings the account's platform declares in ``/accounts`` ``post_settings`` (Reddit: ``subreddit``, ``flair_id``, ``nsfw``, ...). Unknown keys are rejected with 422.

action.description: ``draft`` parks the post for later editing/scheduling; ``schedule`` requires ``scheduled_at`` and queues for publishing.

proposed_publish_at.description: Optional draft-stage suggested publish time (UTC), independent of ``scheduled_at``. Stored as-is — not validated against the future and never queued for publishing; cleared automatically if the post is scheduled.

tags.description: Tag names for the post (created in the workspace's tag list if new). Replaces the current tags.

shorten_links.description: Shorten the links in the post when it is scheduled, one short link per account (and tag them with the workspace's UTM settings). ``null`` follows the workspace's preference, where ``ask`` means no; the workspace's ``never`` setting always wins.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-chosen retry key. Same key + same body → replay first response.

PlatformOverride.description:
Per-account override of the post's title/caption/first_comment.

Mirrors the three form fields the cookie-authenticated UI accepts
(see [apps/composer/views.py:85-96]). Maps to the model's
``platform_specific_*`` columns on ``PlatformPost``.

Each field is independent: omit a field (or send ``null``) to keep
the post's default for that platform. Send a string (including ``""``
to explicitly blank out the value just for this platform) to apply
the override.

social_account_id.description: Must reference an account that is a child of this post.

RecurrenceSpec.description:
Repeat a scheduled post — the same choices as the composer's Repeat control.

The post is the series' first post; copies are generated up to 90 days
ahead at the same local time in the workspace timezone, and carry the
post's content, media and per-platform settings.

frequency.description: ``never`` stops an existing series and removes its upcoming unpublished copies.

interval.description: Repeat every N days / weeks / months.

weekdays.description: Weekly only: days to post on, 0=Monday … 6=Sunday, in the workspace timezone. Defaults to the first post's weekday.

end_date.description: Last date (workspace timezone) a copy may fall on. Can't be combined with ``count``.

count.description: Total posts in the series, the first included. Can't be combined with ``end_date``.

ThreadPart.description: One later part of a thread. The post's ``caption`` and ``media_asset_ids`` are its first part.

media_asset_ids.description: Media for this part. Only on accounts with ``thread_media_per_part=true``.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait after the previous part is live before publishing this one.

is_finisher.description: A closing part (e.g. 'Follow for more'), always published last. At most one.

ThreadPartOverride.description: Per-account caption for one thread part — the part-level ``PlatformOverride.caption``.

social_account_id.description: Must reference an account that is a child of this post.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as ``cursor`` for the next page; null on the last.

internal_notes.description: Private team-only note. Omit (or send null) to leave it unchanged.

parts.description: Replace the thread's later parts (``[]`` makes it a single post). Omit to leave them unchanged. Optional later parts of a thread, in order; the post itself is the first part. Each account publishes them according to its ``thread_mode`` (see /accounts). Scheduling is rejected with 422 when an account can't publish the thread: ``thread_mode='none'``, more than ``thread_max_parts``, a part over ``thread_part_max_length``, or media on a part where ``thread_media_per_part`` is false.

scheduled_at.description: If the post is currently scheduled, this re-times it. Ignored for drafts.

proposed_publish_at.description: Set a draft's suggested publish time (UTC). Sending null is a no-op (cannot clear via PATCH).

recurrence.description: Start or change the repeat of a scheduled post, or stop it with ``frequency='never'``. Changing it replaces the upcoming unpublished copies. Omit (or send null) to leave it unchanged.

post_settings.description: Replace the per-post settings (as on create). Each account takes the keys its platform declares; a declared key left out is cleared. Omit (or send null) to leave them unchanged.

tags.description: Tag names for the post (created in the workspace's tag list if new). Replaces the current tags.

scheduled_at.description: UTC timestamp at which the publisher should fire the post.

recurrence.description: Repeat the post once it is scheduled.

MediaAssetResponse.description:
Single MediaAsset as exposed to the API.

``url`` is whatever ``MediaAsset.file.url`` resolves to — a presigned
URL with a configurable TTL on S3/R2, or a local ``/media/...`` path
on local storage. Agents should treat it as short-lived and always
reference the asset by ``id`` in subsequent calls.

``last_used_at`` is the max ``created_at`` across every Post that
references this asset via ``PostMedia``. It is populated only on
list/detail responses, never on the upload 201.

metrics.description: Same keys as the headline metrics; ``null`` means not available for this account.

OverviewMetricResponse.description: One headline figure summed across the workspace's accounts.

value.description: ``null`` when no account reports this metric. Never ``0`` for missing data.

previous.description: The same figure for the previous equal-length period.

delta.description: Percent change vs. the previous period, calculated by BrightBean Studio over the accounts that reported in both periods. ``null`` when there is nothing to compare.

WorkspaceOverviewResponse.description: Workspace-wide analytics over a date range, with the previous period for comparison.

timezone.description: Workspace timezone the range's days are counted in.

AccountAnalyticsResponse.description: Channel-level analytics summary over a rolling window of days.

connection_status.description: ``connected``, ``token_expiring``, ``disconnected``, or ``error``. Disconnected accounts still return historical analytics, but new data may not be flowing.

days.description: Window size (in days) used for derivation. One of 7, 30, or 90.

analytics_available.description: ``false`` for platforms whose APIs don't expose aggregate analytics (currently LinkedIn Personal, Bluesky, Mastodon). Metric arrays are empty when false.

unavailable_reason.description: Human-readable reason the analytics surface is unavailable, when ``analytics_available`` is false.

hero_metrics.description: Top-line per-channel KPIs. YouTube includes separate likes, comments and shares here.

engagement.description: Engagement-rate card, or ``null`` when the platform lacks a reach-like denominator.

follower_growth.description: New followers / subscribers gained over the window, when the platform reports it.

captured_at.description: Most recent ``captured_at`` across the account's snapshots. ``null`` if no rows yet.

next_sync_eta.description: Approximate next time the background sync will refresh this account. ``null`` for platforms without analytics. Use it to pick a polling delay.

DerivedMetricResponse.description:
A single derived metric over a rolling window.

Mirrors ``apps.analytics.derive.DerivedMetric`` but with a stable wire
shape: agents can rely on every metric carrying the same fields.
The dataclass itself isn't a Pydantic model, so we route through
:meth:`from_derived` rather than letting Ninja convert it implicitly.

value.description: Aggregate value over the current window. Sum for ``count`` metrics, YouTube uses the native whole-period report for every metric, including watch-time totals and averageViewPercentage. Other platforms may average daily percent/minute values.

delta.description: Percent change vs. the previous equal-length window, calculated by BrightBean Studio. ``0.0`` when there is no prior baseline.

series.description: Daily values for the current window, oldest first. ``null`` for a day the platform hasn't reported yet (for example YouTube Analytics' 2-3 day lag), which is not a zero.

calculated_by_brightbean.description: ``true`` when BrightBean Studio calculated ``value`` rather than the platform reporting it: the engagement rate, daily averages, and estimates on supported platforms. Disclosure does not permit prohibited derived metrics. YouTube values are native reports.

averaged.description: ``value`` is BrightBean Studio's average of the platform's daily figures.

estimated.description: ``value`` was estimated by BrightBean Studio from other counts — summed per-post deltas when the platform's account-level analytics weren't available or were older, or differences between follower totals.

comparison_available.description: Whether delta has a complete, nonzero comparison baseline.

parts.description: The component metrics that feed the rate's numerator (likes, comments, shares, …).

formula.description: How the rate was calculated, e.g. ``(Likes + Comments + Shares) ÷ Views``. ``null`` when there was nothing to divide by yet.

PlatformPostAnalyticsResponse.description: Analytics for a single per-platform child of a Post.

analytics_available.description: ``false`` for platforms without analytics. ``true`` for everything else — including drafts and scheduled posts, which simply return empty metric tiles until publish.

metric_tiles.description: One tile per metric this platform reports. Empty until the first snapshot lands.

captured_at.description: Most recent ``captured_at`` across this platform-post's snapshots.

next_sync_eta.description: Approximate next sync time based on the post's age: <24h→+1h, 1-7d→+6h, 7-30d→+1d, 30-90d→+7d, >90d→null (syncs have stopped).

PostAnalyticsResponse.description:
Analytics for a Post, with per-platform breakdown.

Mirrors ``PostResponse``'s parent-Post-with-platform-children shape so
agents that already track ``post_id`` from ``schedule_post`` /
``create_draft`` can poll analytics without learning new IDs.

PostMetricTileResponse.description: One metric tile in the per-post analytics drawer.

value.description: Most recent snapshot value for this metric on this post.

series.description: Daily sparkline since publish — one entry per day with a recorded snapshot.

is_primary.description: True for the platform's default headline metric (e.g. ``views`` for YouTube).

ReportRunResponse.description: One build of a report: its status, period and (when ready) headline figures.

error.description: Why the run failed, when it did.

emailed_to.description: How many recipients the PDF was emailed to.

summary.description: The report's 'what changed and what to do next' text, once ready.

metrics.description: Headline figures once ready: ``key``, ``label``, ``value`` (display), ``delta`` (percent) per metric.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as ``cursor`` for the next page; null on the last.

supported.description: False when the network has no official way to read other profiles.
